We need to identify highest-risk bug in round 1 (previous answer). The bug likely is in restoreSession: missing restoration of thread IDs and threadToAgentId mapping, causing inconsistency. The highest-risk bug is that restoreSession discards thread IDs and threadToAgentId, leading to pending turns referencing missing threads, causing errors during resume or reconnect.

We need to refine patch plan for round 2 with constraint: public message contracts must not change. So we cannot change message schemas. We need to adjust restoreSession to correctly restore thread IDs and threadToAgentId from saved snapshot, without altering public contracts.

We need to keep same message contracts (i.e., ServerMessage types unchanged). So we can modify internal handling.

We need to produce a patch plan: smallest safe changes to fix bug.

We need to identify the exact bug: In restoreSession, after loading saved snapshot, they set this.threadIds = { gameplayByAgentId: {} }; they ignore saved.threadIds.threadIds.gameplayByAgentId and builder. They also clear threadToAgentId. They should restore thread IDs and mapping.

Also they need to resume threads for existing session: they have startThreadsForExistingSession used in startSession when simulation exists and no threads. In restoreSession they should also resume threads using saved thread IDs.

But we cannot change public contracts; we can add code to load thread IDs from saved snapshot.

Implementation: In restoreSession, after setting simulation and agentConfigs, we should set this.threadIds = saved.threadIds (or at least copy gameplayByAgentId and builder). Also need to populate threadToAgentId mapping: for each agentId in saved.threadIds.gameplayByAgentId, we have mapping to agentId (maybe stored elsewhere). In saved snapshot, there is no mapping; but we can reconstruct mapping using agentConfigs? In saved snapshot, we have saved.simulation.agents list with ids. We can map each threadId to agentId using saved.threadIds.gameplayByAgentId.

Thus we can set this.threadToAgentId = new Map(); for each [agentId, threadId] in saved.threadIds.gameplayByAgentId, set threadToAgentId.set(threadId, agentId). Also set builder thread if present.

Also need to ensure that pendingTurns may reference turn IDs that were stored; but pendingTurns is cleared? In restoreSession they clear pendingTurns? They don't clear pendingTurns; they just set activeTurn null, schedulerIndex 0, etc. pendingTurns may still have entries from previous session? In saved snapshot, pendingTurns not saved (not part of SessionSnapshot). So pendingTurns should be cleared. In restoreSession they didn't clear pendingTurns. They should clear pendingTurns to avoid stale collectors. In startSession they clear pendingTurns. In restoreSession they should also clear pendingTurns.

But the bug is about thread IDs causing inconsistency. So patch: in restoreSession, after loading saved, set threadIds = saved.threadIds (or copy). Also ensure threadToAgentId mapping.

Also need to ensure that if saved.simulation exists, we have saved.threadIds.threadIds.gameplayByAgentId and builder. If saved.simulation missing (i.e., only seed), we may need to start threads for existing session? In that case, we have only one agent (agent-1). We could start threads for that agent and builder? In startSession they start threads for each agent and builder. In restoreSession for seed case they create new simulation with one agent and then they should also start threads for that agent and builder. However they currently set threadIds empty and not start threads. That could cause missing builder thread. But they have logic in primeCodexModelCatalog that checks if simulation && no thread IDs then startThreadsForExistingSession. In restoreSession after setting simulation, they set phase to running and then later primeCodexModelCatalog will be called? Actually start() calls restoreSession then startTimers then primeCodexModelCatalog. In restoreSession they set phase to running, but they haven't started threads. Then primeCodexModelCatalog will be called after startTimers? In start() they call restoreSession before startTimers, then startTimers, then void this.primeCodexModelCatalog(). So after restoreSession, primeCodexModelCatalog will be called. In primeCodexModelCatalog, they check if simulation && Object.keys(this.threadIds.gameplayByAgentId).length === 0 && !this.threadIds.builder then await this.startThreadsForExistingSession(). Since threadIds are empty, they will start threads for existing session (i.e., start threads for each agent and builder). That's good.
